subject: Civic Education
competence: Works with understanding the rights of the child and his duties by analyzing safeguarding institutions.
lesson: Expresses the functions of institutions that work towards safeguarding the rights of the child: Mock Local Council / Pradeshiya Sabha Session: Competency Level 8.2.2
unique_learning_outcome: Expresses the functions of institutions that work towards safeguarding the rights of the child.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: The teacher greets the 40 students and projects an authentic Sri Lankan newspaper clipping regarding a child welfare intervention by the Department of Probation and Child Care Services. The teacher prompts the class: 'Imagine a local child facing hardship in our community—which official institutions step in to protect them and how do they coordinate?' The teacher invites quick initial student shouts from everyday experience, instantly transitioning the room into 8 teams of 5 students each to begin the mock council session.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher circulates among the 8 teams, distributing specific institutional case scenarios involving child rights violations and protection responses. The facilitator ensures that every student within the groups of five assumes their designated role: Leader, Scribe, Timekeeper, Spokesperson, or Civic Investigator. The teacher prompts teams to examine the jurisdictional mandates of the National Child Protection Authority, Police Women and Children Bureau, and Probation Department.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students organize their desks into 8 collaborative team circles and assign their specific roles without any bystanders. The Scribe and Leader review the distributed case brief, while the Civic Investigator cross-references the text with textbook facts about child safeguarding institutions. The Timekeeper sets a strict 10-minute countdown to formulate their initial institutional response strategy.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Pradeshiya Sabha role cards, institution case brief handouts, notebook, and pens

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher acts as a mobile facilitator, moving dynamically between the 8 teams to observe interactions and pose scaffolding questions such as 'How does the Department of Probation coordinate with local voluntary organizations in this scenario?' The teacher challenges teams to ensure their proposed civic resolution accurately mirrors the legal functions of child protection bodies.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Team members actively debate the case scenario, proposing specific actions that institutions like UNICEF or the Sri Lanka Police should take. The Scribe records the agreed-upon resolution and supporting reasons on chart paper, while the Spokesperson rehearses the upcoming delivery. The Civic Investigator checks the group's arguments against official statutory duties of child welfare agencies.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_method: Collaborative Mock Council Deliberation & Resolution Drafting
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chart paper, colored markers, institutional function reference sheets

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher moderates a rapid-fire plenary session where designated team spokespersons summarize their mock council resolutions. The teacher guides peer evaluation by asking the rest of the class to verify whether the stated institutional functions are legally accurate, finally synthesizing the core takeaways on the chalkboard.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Team spokespersons present their concise civic decisions and justifications to the whole class within a strict time limit. Remaining students actively evaluate the presentations from their seats, noting down complementary institutional functions in their student notebooks.

summary: The teacher synthesizes that safeguarding child rights is a collaborative duty shared by specialized state institutions including the Department of Probation and Child Care Services, the Women and Children's Bureau, and international bodies like UNICEF. Students consolidate their understanding that effective community protection requires active coordination and legal awareness.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative evaluation is conducted by assessing group accuracy in identifying institutional functions, clarity of role execution during the mock council, and the quality of peer feedback during plenary presentations.
post_activity: Each student writes down one specific safeguarding function performed by the Department of Probation on a slip of paper and drops it into the team box during a rapid 5-minute in-class exit check.
